title: Shared definitions
description: Building blocks referenced by the other schemas in docs/schemas/. Not an output shape on its own.

timestamp.description: A UTC timestamp as stored in SQLite: 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP's format). Rows written before GitHub issue #202 may carry an ISO-8601 form with 'T' and a UTC offset, hence only the leading date and time are pinned.

sweepCompletedAt.description: When the support sweep's queue emptied (support_probe_job_generator_runs.completed_at): its last probe settled, or a later sweep took over its last outstanding probes. Null while it runs, and for a sweep that ended before completion times were recorded (GitHub issue #235).

nullableCount.description: A count, or null when there is no measurement (never a stand-in for zero).

importId.description: imports.import_id - the import's creation time as Unix epoch seconds.

nullablePercentage.description: A raw percentage, or null when either side of the ratio is unknown (no domain share selected, or no measurement for this provider in that import).

nullableZones.description: The zones an import read (GitHub issue #218), by zone name without the trailing dot (e.g. 'com'), sorted; null when unknown (an import from before they were recorded).

nullableSamplePercent.description: The percentage of the zones' domains an import sampled for scanning (GitHub issue #218); 100 is a census. null when unknown (an import from before it was recorded) or when its zones were sampled at different rates.

shareSource.description: Where a domain share's numbers came from: 'live' (computed from the import's results) or 'snapshot' (provider_import_share - the import was pruned by hygiene).

settingsStatus.description: Outcome of the newest settings run that settled one of the provider's Domain Connect URLs (GitHub issue #272): 'ok' if one answered (possibly after retries), 'failed' once every retry was used up or the host was given up. A request still retrying changes nothing. null before the first settled run.

settingsErrorKind.description: Why the newest settled settings run failed: 'http_error' (an unusable HTTP answer, every retry used up) or 'dead' (the host was given up: unreachable for a long time, or a permanent failure such as an invalid TLS certificate). null unless settings status is 'failed'.

supportStatus.description: Outcome of the newest completed support sweep covering the provider (GitHub issue #272), from each probe's final outcome after its retries: 'ok' (every probe answered), 'partial' (some answered, some failed), 'error' (none answered) or 'dead' (the host was given up during the sweep). A sweep still running changes nothing. null before the first completed sweep.

supportAnswered.description: Probes of the newest completed support sweep covering the provider that ended with an answer (supported or not supported); null before the first completed sweep.

supportFailed.description: Probes of the newest completed support sweep covering the provider that ended in an error after their retries; null before the first completed sweep.

publicSupportBucketColumns.description: The support buckets, results only (GitHub issues #265/#270/#271): supported (the latest conclusive probe answered 200) / not supported (it answered 404) - a failed or queued re-probe changes neither - and undetermined, the rest of the row's total (no conclusive answer yet: never probed, queued, retrying or failed - probe progress is report.py status's, never a result), each with its percentage of the row's total. The three counts sum to the total.

templateChangeColumns.description: The change of the supported templates (GitHub issue #219), for leaderboards. A change is null, never 0, when nothing measured the reference point: no such sweep, or it started before the DNS provider (a stack: its first deployment) was first seen.

supported_templates_change.description: Change in supported templates from the previous sweep to the latest one, by the support history's replay (support confirmed by a 200 until a 404 withdraws it).

supported_templates_change_90d.description: Change in supported templates from the newest sweep that started at least 90 days before the latest one, to the latest one; replayed like supported_templates_change.

templateTrendColumns.description: Distinct templates any deployment of a stack supports, and their change (templateChangeColumns).

supported_templates.description: Templates (service provider, service id) any deployment supports now, each once.

servedCountColumns.description: What the supported templates' answers served (GitHub issue #281), per DNS provider (a stack: summed over its deployments). Each counts supported templates whose latest 200 carried it; templates supported before the provider was probed for it since are in none.

with_version_count.description: Supported templates whose answer named a version (served_version not null).

full_template_count.description: Supported templates answered with the full template (response_kind 'template').

morphed_count.description: Full templates differing from the repository's (template_match 'morphed').

outdated_count.description: Full templates with a version below the repository's (template_match 'outdated').

servedVersion.description: The version the DNS provider's latest 200 named (GitHub issue #281); null when it named none, or when the provider was not probed for the template since it began to be recorded.

responseKind.description: What the DNS provider's latest 200 carried (GitHub issue #281): 'empty' (no usable body), 'version' (its version only) or 'template' (the full template); null when not recorded yet.

templateMatch.description: For a full template (response_kind 'template'): 'match' (equal to the repository's, canonicalised), 'morphed' (altered), 'outdated' (its version below the repository's); null otherwise, or when the repository template is not recorded yet.

sweepHistoryRow.description: One support sweep (support_probe_job_generator_runs row), oldest first.

change.description: Difference to the previous row's count (to 0 for the first row).

report.description: The one JSON shape every report shares (GitHub issue #204): notes, then tables keyed by id, and no other key. Each report's schema pins its own tables' ids, column keys (in display order) and row types on top of this. Titles, column headers and note texts are display text: only their type is pinned, their wording may change without notice (docs/EXPORT_FORMAT.md, Versioning and compatibility). A row holds raw values only, keyed by exactly its table's column keys.

exportGeneratedAt.description: When the export ran, UTC, to the second: the manifest's generated_at, which every file of one release carries.

exportFile.description: A list or card file of the static export (export.py, GitHub issue #211): the report shape plus the release's generated_at (the export adds it; report.py's JSON never has it). Not closed: each export schema adds its report's notes/tables constraints and closes the object with unevaluatedProperties: false.

reportBody.description: The report shape's keys without closing the object: the base of report (which closes it) and of exportFile (which adds generated_at).

notes.description: Free-text context for the tables, e.g. which import the domain columns describe.

tables.description: The report's tables keyed by table id (unique within the report; not shown in txt/markdown), in report order.

columns.description: The table's columns in display order: each row's key (the contract) and its txt/markdown header (display text).

footer.description: A summary row (e.g. TOTAL) keyed like the rows; null when the table has none.

oneRow.description: The rows of a table that is one record (GitHub issue #204): exactly one row, its columns the record's fields, so a reader gets a dict (rows[0].<field>). txt/markdown show such a table transposed, one line per field.

shareNotes.description: The share-weighted reports' one note: which import (id, status, live or snapshot, domains scanned) the domain columns describe, or that no import matched and they are blank.
